correctness.rationale: From the actual frozen RESULT.md derive c_F=||Omega b||²/[(Omega b)^T Omega Ab] and c_G=[(Omega Ab)^T Omega b]/||Omega Ab||². Orthogonally decompose Av=a v+d w. Independent standard normal sketches of v and w make (u^T z)/||u||²=Z/sqrt(chi²_ell)=T_ell/sqrt(ell), so c_F^{-1}=a+(d/sqrt ell)T_ell. Rotating to Av/sqrt(m) yields c_G=a/m+(d/(m sqrt ell))T'_ell. The reciprocal denominator density is positive at zero for every finite ell when d>0, giving the displayed 2 f_Y(0)/t tail and all |c_F|^q divergences q>=1; the exact A-orthogonal energy decomposition transfers this to expected squared error. For ell>2 Student variance d²/[m²(ell-2)] and residual expansion give ||b||²(d²/m)(ell-1)/(ell-2); all moment thresholds and eigenvector boundary d=0 were reconstructed. The inspected standard-library verifier samples exact coefficient identities, not rare-tail proofs.

value.rationale: An exact universal separation between the unconditional moments of two established one-step Krylov projections is mathematically motivated by rare projection singularities and high-probability safeguards. Infinite A-error at every finite oversampling size is a concrete all-parameter phenomenon, with exact tail constant and finite-risk comparator; it is not an arbitrary small example or a renamed normal-ratio identity.

final_claim: For a non-eigenvector SPD one-step Krylov problem with any finite Gaussian sketch size ell>=2, the sketched FOM coefficient is a reciprocal shifted Student-t variable and has a positive-density pole, hence infinite absolute moments of all orders >=1 and infinite expected squared A-energy solution error; the sketched GMRES coefficient is affine Student with finite variance precisely for ell>2 and an exact expected unsketched squared residual.
limitations: Real SPD, b non-eigenvector, Gaussian i.i.d., exactly one unregularized step; infinity is unconditional and not a failure of conditional embedding guarantees.
